Lucknow Respondent :- Smt. Ramawati @ Saroj Kumari And Ors.
Counsel for Appellant :- Prabhakari Tiwari,Akhter Abbas,Ambika Prasad,J.B. Singh Counsel for Respondent :- Durgesh Kumar Singh,Suresh Kumar Yadav Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.

1. Heard Sri Ambika Prasad, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Durgesh Kumar Singh,
learned counsel for the claimant-respondents no. 1 to 6.

During the pendency of the present appeal,
the respondent no. 3 had died and since the legal heirs are already on record, accordingly,
appropriate endorsement has been made in the array of parties.

2. The instant appeal has been preferred under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 18.03.2011 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Additional District Judge, Court No. 9, Barabanki in Claim Petition no. 204 of 2009 whereby the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs. 21,34,378/- along with 6% interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till the actual payment to the claimant-respondents.

sentences.text: The record would indicate that by means of order dated 05.07.2011 while admitting the appeal,
notices

were issued to the respondents and as an interim measure it was provided that the entire amount under the award shall be deposited before this Court out of which a sum of Rs.
5,00,000/-was released in favour of the claimants-respondents.
4. While assailing the award dated 18.03.2011, the learned counsel for the appellant has primarily attacked on the findings of issue no. (i).

It has been urged by learned counsel for the appellant that the manner in which the accident is said to have occurred and as proved by the claimants, there are certain inherent contradictions in the testimony of P.W. 1 and P.W. 2 which if taken together would give rise to a question mark over the occurrence of the accident in the first place.

5. It is further urged that a specific defence was raised by the learned counsel for the appellant that the accident did not occur with the Bus belonging to the appellant and it is in the aforesaid backdrop if the testimony of the witnesses is seen, it would indicate that neither the P.W. 1 had seen the accident or could identify the bus in question and moreover the P.W. 2 who is alleged to have seen the accident but in his testimony, there are contradictions which raises a doubt over the credibility of such a witness.
In the aforesaid backdrop where the accident has not been proved awarding the sum in favour of the claimants-respondents against the appellant is not justified.

6. The learned counsel for the respondent while refuting the aforesaid submissions has submitted that the P.w. 2 was an eye-witness who clearly deposed that he was having tea at a roadside stall and he had seen the accident where the bus was involved.
The eye-witness identified the bus in question and the accident in furtherance whereof, the injured was taken to the hospital where he succumbed to his injuries two days later.

7. It is also pointed out that the First Information Report was lodged and a charge sheet was also filed against the driver of the offending bus and the aforesaid facts as well as the circumstances clearly indicated that the accident had occurred which was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the appellant, accordingly, the award as made by the Tribunal does not require any interference and the appeal deserves to be dismissed.

8. The Court has heard the learned counsel for the parties and also perused the material on record,
however, before adverting to the respective submissions of learned counsel for the parties, certain brief facts giving rise to the instant appeal are being noticed hereinafter:-
9.

It is the case of the claimants that their father namely Shiv Kumar Singh on 11.08.2008 while he was preparing to go o the college where he was teaching and at around 07:30 AM had left his house and while he had reached the Bhitaria Crossing at about 08:45 AM, it is at that point of time that a bus bearing No. UP 32 AM 8030 which was being driven rashly and negligently hit Sri Shiv Kumar from the back which caused grievous injuries.
The injured was immediately taken to Akansha Nursing Home from where he was referred to a higher center at Medical College at Lucknow where he expired on 20th August, 2008.

It is in respect of the aforesaid death that the claim petition No.
204 of 2009 came to be filed before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Barabanki.

2 10.

The claim petition came to be contested by the appellants by filing a written statement wherein a plea was raised that the bus in question was not involved in the accident, inasmuch as, the bus left the Lucknow-Kaiserbagh Depot at about 07:30 AM and it takes about two or two and a half hours to reach Bhitaria Crossing and as such the said accident with the bus in question was not possible at about 08:45 AM as the bus could not reach that place in such a short span of time.
11.
It was also urged before the Tribunal that the amount as sought by the claimants was on the higher side and for the aforesaid reasons, the claim petition deserves to be dismissed.

12. The Tribunal after exchange of pleadings framed two issues, however, for the instant appeal it is only the issue no. 1 which is under challenge and i.e. as to whether the accident occurred on 11.08.2008 at about 08:45 AM with the bus belonging to the appellant bearing no. UP 32 AM 8030 and whether its driver was driving rashly and negligently.

13. In support of their respective contentions, the parties have led their evidences and three witnesses were examined on behalf of the claimants whereas three witnesses were also examined on behalf of the appellant.

The Tribunal while considering the issue no. (i) and assessing the evidence led by the parties both oral and documentary found that the accident was occasioned on account of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending bus bearing No. UP 32 AM 803.

It is taking the aforesaid findings forward that the Tribunal went ahead to assess the compensation and thereafter by means of its award dated 18.03.2011 awarded a sum of Rs. 21, 34, 378/- along with 6%
interest from the date of the application till the date of its actual payment.

It is this award which is under challenge on the ground as already noticed hereinabove:-
14.

Having considered the aforesaid factual background as well as the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, this Court finds that in so far as the plea raised by the learned counsel for the appellant that the accident could not occur in a short spam of time as the bus usually takes about two and two and a half hour from Lucknow-Kaiserbagh Depot to reach Bhitaria Crossing and this was taken as a sheet anchor for the defence

, however, in light of the evidence which was led including the assessment made by the Tribunal, it would indicate that the witnesses of the appellant who were cross-examined including the driver had made a statement that at the given point of time he had reached the Safdarjang location by the Bhitaria crossing where the alleged accident is said to have taken place is merely 15 kms.

15. The estimation by which it has been stated that it usually takes two or two and a half hours to reach Bhitaria Crossing is on the premise that generally taking into account the traffic which is available, the general tendency of stopping the bus on the route and taking passengers for de-boarding the bus from the bus including the stoppages at certain check points involves consumption of time and it is in view thereof that the estimation of two or two and a half hours has been given, however, from the perusal of the testimony of the appellant-witnesses before the Tribunal it would reveal that there was no averment made by any of the witness of the appellant including the driver that as on the given date i.e. 11.08.2008 where did the bus stop for checking at any check-post, the driver in question ought to have clarified the same but his testimony is completely silent on the aforesaid point.

No details about traffic density, stoppage of the bus for U.P State Rd. Transport Corp. Lucknow vs Smt. Ramawati @ Saroj Kumari And Ors. on 12 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145260958/
3 boarding or de-boarding of passengers or for checking has been given nor as to how much time was taken for the aforesaid reason in the testimony, coupled with the fact that the driver stated that the location of the bus at the relevant hour was in between Barabanki and Safdarzang, which is about 15 Kms. from Bhitariya Crossing and it is not quite abnormal for the bus to have reached at the given time especially when time as mentioned was by estimation and not by precision.
16.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Be that as it may, the distance between Lucknow to Bhitaria Crossing is said to be about 65 Kms.

and covering the said distance within a period of 1 and 1/2 hours is not quite un-imaginable which may draw an adverse inference upon the testimony given by the claimant-witnesses and moreover the time is only by estimation and not a precise timing which is so absurd which may throw the entire account in grave doubts.

17. On the other hand if the testimony of the claimant-witness is seen, it would indicate that P.W. 1 is the son of the deceased who had stated that he had received the information regarding the accident and had reached the site where his father had been taken to Akansha Nursing Home thereafter he was shifted to Trauma Center at Lucknow where he succumbed to his injuries.

18. Admittedly, P.W. 1 is not the eye-witness but nevertheless P.W. 2 who was the eye-witness had clearly deposed that he was sitting at the road side hotel sipping a cup of tea, it is during this time,
he had seen the accident and he clearly identified that the bus belonging to the U.P.S.R.T.C. and it was being driven rashly and negligently which caused the accident wherein the injured Sri Shiv Kumar received injuries which further led to his death.

19. Having taken note of the cross-examination of the aforesaid P.W.2, emphasis has been made by the learned counsel for the appellant to point out certain contradictions but nevertheless minor contradictions are not going to affect the credibility of the witness where the foundational facts have been reiterated even in the cross-examination.
There is nothing which has been elicited from the cross-examination which may caste an adverse aspersion over the testimony of the P.W. 2.
There is no denial regarding the lodging of the First Information Report against the bus driver, filing of charge sheet and trial faced by him.
The P.W. 2 is a independent witness and all these facts have been considered by the Tribunal and foundational facts have been found to be confirmed.

20. Having considered the matter in a holistic manner, this Court finds that the findings recorded by the Tribunal on issue no. (i) does not suffer from any error which may persuade this Court to intervene.
21.

Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court finds that the award dated 18.03.2011 does not suffer from any error and the submissions of the appellant does not find favour with this Court.
22.
In view of the aforesaid, the appeal is dismissed.
The award dated 18.03.2011 is affirmed.
The amount deposited before this Court shall be remitted to the Tribunal in faour of the claimants as per the award.
In the facts and circumstances, there shall be no order as to costs.
